name: obol_local_pivot_2026_09
description: Post-foothold host and network enumeration for pivot-candidate discovery.

source.name: O.B.O.L local pivot methodology
source.notes: Small OS-aware local commands run through existing SSH/WinRM proof channels after access is proven.

actions.title: Enumerate Linux interfaces
actions.hypothesis: A Linux foothold can expose additional interfaces or subnets that may become pivot candidates.

commands.note: Use the validated plaintext credential to run a non-interactive interface check over SSH.
commands.run: sshpass -p {{password}} ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=8 {{user}}@{{target}} ip -o addr show

commands.note: On-target: list all network interfaces and IPv4/IPv6 addresses to spot a second internal NIC.
On-target fallback when iproute2 is missing on minimal containers or legacy hosts.

actions.title: Enumerate Linux routes
actions.hypothesis: Routes from a foothold identify adjacent networks worth validating before building a tunnel.

commands.note: Collect route table evidence without claiming the route is reachable through a working pivot yet.
commands.run: sshpass -p {{password}} ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=8 {{user}}@{{target}} ip route

commands.note: On-target: display the kernel routing table to identify reachable internal subnets.
On-target legacy route table check.

actions.title: Enumerate Linux ARP neighbors
actions.hypothesis: Neighbor cache entries are weak but useful hints for hosts near the foothold.

commands.note: Record observed neighbors as host-scoped hints only.
commands.run: sshpass -p {{password}} ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=8 {{user}}@{{target}} ip neigh show

commands.note: On-target: inspect the ARP/neighbor cache for live internal hosts this machine has recently talked to.

actions.title: Enumerate Linux DNS servers
actions.hypothesis: Resolver configuration can identify internal DNS infrastructure for follow-up enumeration.

commands.note: Read resolver configuration through the existing non-interactive SSH channel.
On-target: read DNS resolvers, search domains, and static host mappings.

actions.title: Enumerate Windows interfaces
actions.hypothesis: A Windows WinRM foothold can expose additional NICs, DNS servers, or subnets that may become pivot candidates.

commands.note: Use WinRM exec through NetExec so output is captured and parsed like every other run.
On-target (cmd.exe): list all adapters, IPs, DNS suffixes, and gateways.
On-target (PowerShell): structured adapter and gateway summary.

actions.title: Enumerate Windows routes
actions.hypothesis: The Windows route table can reveal internal subnets before any tunnel exists.

commands.note: Collect route evidence only; a route does not prove a working tunnel.
On-target (cmd.exe): print the IPv4 and IPv6 routing tables to spot internal subnets.

commands.run: powershell -ep bypass -c "Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object {$_.NextHop -ne '0.0.0.0' -or $_.DestinationPrefix -match '^(10|172|192)\.'} | Format-Table DestinationPrefix,NextHop,InterfaceAlias"
commands.note: On-target (PowerShell): filter IPv4 routes to internal subnets and gateways.

actions.title: Enumerate Windows ARP neighbors
actions.hypothesis: ARP cache entries can identify nearby internal hosts to validate through a later tunnel.

commands.note: Record neighbor hints without treating them as discovered targets.
On-target (cmd.exe): inspect the ARP table per interface for live internal neighbors.

commands.run: powershell -ep bypass -c "Get-NetNeighbor -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object State -ne 'Unreachable' | Format-Table IPAddress,LinkLayerAddress,State,InterfaceAlias"
commands.note: On-target (PowerShell): list active IPv4 neighbors.

actions.title: Enumerate Windows listening sockets
actions.hypothesis: Listening sockets give local service context and can help pick tunnel/port-forward targets later.

commands.note: Capture local listener evidence for later route-aware pivot planning.
On-target (cmd.exe): list listening TCP ports and owning PIDs, looking for 127.0.0.1-only services to port-forward.

commands.run: powershell -ep bypass -c "Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Select-Object LocalAddress,LocalPort,OwningProcess | Sort-Object LocalPort"
commands.note: On-target (PowerShell): structured list of listening TCP ports.

actions.title: Ligolo-ng TUN Interface Pivot and Internal Subnet Routing
actions.hypothesis: Target foothold has dual-homed network interfaces or access to an internal subnet. Deploying the Ligolo-ng agent establishes a reverse tunnel to the Kali ligolo-proxy, allowing transparent subnet routing via a local TUN interface.
actions.proves: establishes a live routed TUN interface proxying raw TCP/UDP packets into target internal subnet
actions.does_not_prove: compromise of hosts on internal subnet until subsequent enumeration and attacks succeed

report.finding: Internal Subnet Access Established via Routed TUN Pivot

commands.run: sudo ip tuntap add user {{kali_user}} mode tun dev ligolo && sudo ip link set ligolo up && ligolo-proxy -selfcert -laddr 0.0.0.0:11601
commands.note: Initialize ligolo TUN interface on Kali and launch ligolo-proxy listener.
Execute ligolo agent on foothold host to establish reverse tunnel session back to Kali.

commands.run: sudo ip route add {{internal_subnet}} dev ligolo
commands.note: Add routing entry directing internal subnet traffic through the active ligolo TUN interface.
